system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Basis:** Seller Update positions and Disclosure Letter only. I have not seen the full SPA text, the data room documents (DD-002 to DD-012) or the funds flow. Clause references follow the Seller's numbering. Statutory points should be checked against current law before relying on them externally.

---

## 1. Overall assessment

The cover email calls the package "fair and balanced." It is not. Taken together, the positions shift almost all known and unknown risk to Wattlebridge.

- **Known risks:** The Disclosure Letter identifies at least six live issues worth well over AUD 4 million combined. These are Bluefen (30% of revenue), Riverlark (AUD 3.2m debt), Ironquay IP, bonuses (AUD 420k plus on-costs), the DD-006 privacy incident, and Sandbar (AUD 330k). The Seller Update either understates these ("addressed," "adequate," "not expected to be material," "ordinary course") or leaves them for later.
- **Unknown risks:** General disclosure, the constructive-knowledge bar, the catch-all limitations and the fundamental warranties being capped all point the same way. Wattlebridge would have little practical recovery even for problems no one has yet found.

The Disclosure Letter itself is more candid than the Seller Update. On several points it contradicts the Update's characterisation. We should use the Seller's own disclosures against those positions.

The Disclosure Letter is stated as at **22 September 2026**. Today is 5 November 2026, so it is about six weeks stale. Several matters are time-sensitive, especially DD-006, and need a current update.

---

## 2. Structural and liability regime issues

### 2.1 General liability cap: 20% (AUD 4.8m), clause 12.1
- **Why it hurts us:** 20% is at the low end for a private-seller deal. It is also lower than the known exposure listed in section 3 of this note. Those known issues should sit outside the cap through specific indemnities. Even so, 20% leaves little headroom for unknown breaches.
- **Push back:**
  - Ask for 30 to 50% if there is no W&I insurance.
  - If W&I is used, a lower seller cap is more acceptable, but the known matters must then be carved out with specific indemnities, since W&I will exclude them.
- **Security:** Harbourglass appears to be a fund or investment vehicle that may distribute proceeds after Completion. Ask for one of the following:
  - a retention or escrow (for example 10 to 15% of price for the general claims period, plus specific retentions for Ironquay and DD-006); or
  - a parent or fund guarantee.

### 2.2 Thresholds, clause 12.2
- **De minimis of AUD 25,000:** Acceptable in principle, but related claims arising from the same facts must aggregate. Ask for a lower figure (around AUD 10k to 15k).
- **Basket of AUD 250,000, excess only:** This is about 1.04% of price and works as a **deductible**, so Wattlebridge absorbs the first AUD 250k in every case.
  - Push for a **tipping basket**: once the threshold is crossed, the full amount is recoverable from the first dollar.
  - Push for a threshold of around 0.5% (AUD 120k).
- **Carve-outs:** Neither threshold should apply to fundamental warranties, the tax covenant or specific indemnities.

### 2.3 Time limits and the catch-all, clauses 12.3 and 13
- **18 months for general warranties:** Workable, but 24 months is preferable. That gives two full audit cycles under our ownership.
- **"Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise": reject this.**
  - It is a drafting trap. Any carve-out we fail to spell out by default sweeps the specific indemnities, the tax covenant, fundamental warranties, completion obligations, price adjustment and leakage claims into the cap, thresholds and 18-month limit.
  - Reverse the default. Limitations apply **only** to general Warranty Claims unless expressly extended.
- **Tax claims:** These need a time limit tied to the ATO amendment period plus a buffer, typically 5 to 7 years.

### 2.4 Fundamental warranties (title and capacity) under the general cap and time limit
- **Reject.** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason. Title is the whole asset being bought.
  - **Cap:** 100% of the price.
  - **Time limit:** At least 6 years. This aligns with the NSW limitation period for contract claims and is longer if the SPA is executed as a deed.
  - No thresholds should apply.
- **Title evidence: the share register at DD-012 alone is insufficient.** We need:
  - ASIC company extract and historic search, reconciled to the register;
  - review of the constitution and any shareholder agreement for pre-emptive rights;
  - confirmation that there are no options, convertible notes, ESOP or phantom equity (relevant given the DD-005 bonuses);
  - PPSR search against the Seller and the Company, and a check of whether **Riverlark's security includes a share mortgage or featherweight charge over the Seller's shares**;
  - delivery at Completion of share certificates, signed transfers and releases of any share security.
- The Disclosure Letter (para 10) itself says no verification has been completed. That is effectively an invitation to do it.

### 2.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature," clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5
- **Reject the blanket application.** Carve-outs must include:
  - fraud, dishonesty, wilful misconduct and wilful concealment by the Seller, the Company or their officers. Liability for fraud cannot validly be excluded in any event, but the SPA should say so expressly;
  - specific indemnities and the tax covenant;
  - completion and payment obligations, price adjustment and leakage;
  - restraints and confidentiality;
  - equitable remedies such as specific performance and injunction.
- **Non-reliance:** Australian courts treat entire-agreement and non-reliance clauses as relevant evidence, but not necessarily a complete bar, to claims for misleading or deceptive conduct under the Australian Consumer Law (s 18). Even so, a broad clause makes those claims harder. It should not cover the Warranties, the Disclosure Letter or written replies to due diligence requests.

### 2.6 Disclosure: general disclosure of the data room and public registers (Schedule 7; Disclosure Letter paras 1.1 and 1.2)
- **This is the single most damaging structural point.** If every fact anywhere in the data room, the Accounts, the statutory registers and public records qualifies every warranty, the warranties become close to worthless.
- **Push back:**
  - Only **specific disclosures** made against specific warranties should qualify those warranties.
  - Disclosures must be **"fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its likely effect."**
  - Delete general disclosure of public records. As a fallback, limit it to searches actually conducted on specified dates, with results listed.
  - The data room should be disclosed only via an agreed index on USB, and only to the extent specifically referenced and fairly disclosed.
- **Disclosures must never qualify** fundamental warranties, the tax covenant or the specific indemnities. Otherwise, for example, the Bluefen and DD-006 disclosures would neutralise the very indemnities designed to cover them.
- **No updating:** There should be no ability to update disclosures between signing and Completion. If updating is conceded, any material new disclosure should give Wattlebridge a termination right and should not cure the breach for damages purposes.
- **Para 1.4 (non-admission):** Acceptable, provided it does not dilute specific indemnities.

### 2.7 Buyer knowledge bar, clause 8.3
- **Reject.** The clause bars claims for anything the Buyer **or its advisers** knew, *including anything "discoverable"* from the data room or public records. That is constructive knowledge and, combined with general disclosure, effectively eliminates warranty protection.
- **Replace with a pro-buyer clause:** Warranties are not affected by any investigation or knowledge, actual, constructive or imputed, of the Buyer or its advisers.
- **Fallback only:** A bar limited to the *actual* knowledge of named Wattlebridge deal team individuals, confined to the specific breach and its amount.
- **Why the express clause matters:** Without an express "knowledge does not affect claims" clause, Australian courts may treat a buyer's pre-contract knowledge as relevant to recoverable loss. Silence is therefore not a safe position for us either.

### 2.8 Tax and IP "settled under the general regime"
- **Reject.**
- **Tax:** Require a standalone **tax indemnity or covenant** for all pre-Completion taxes, including payroll tax, superannuation guarantee charge, PAYG and GST. It should:
  - be capped at the price;
  - run for the ATO amendment period plus a buffer;
  - not be subject to thresholds or disclosure;
  - include conduct-of-claims provisions.
- **IP:** For an analytics business, IP ownership is core value. Treat the key IP warranties (ownership, no infringement, no open-source contamination, employee and contractor assignment) as **quasi-fundamental**, with a higher cap and longer survival.

---

## 3. Specific known issues

### 3.1 Bluefen: 30% of revenue, change-control consent (DD-002; clauses 3 and 6.3; Disclosure Letter para 2)
- **Contradiction:** The Seller Update says consent is "addressed." The Disclosure Letter says **no final written consent has been obtained and there is no evidence the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied.**
- **Risks in the Seller's proposal:**
  - Reasonable endeavours is a weak obligation.
  - Treating the consent as satisfied "on delivery of written consent" could be met by a **conditional** consent. Bluefen could, for example, demand price concessions, reserve termination rights or impose conditions under 11.3. Wattlebridge would then be forced to complete.
- **Push for:**
  - A **condition precedent**: Bluefen's written consent, unconditional or on terms acceptable to the Buyer acting reasonably, with all 11.3 conditions satisfied or waived by Bluefen. The condition should be **waivable only by the Buyer**.
  - An "all reasonable endeavours" obligation on the Seller, with Buyer participation in communications.
  - No concessions to Bluefen without Buyer consent.
  - A sunset date with a Buyer termination right.
- **Where Bluefen accepts but extracts value:** Consider a price adjustment or specific indemnity for lost or diminished Bluefen revenue over 12 to 24 months.

### 3.2 Riverlark facility: about AUD 3.2m (DD-003; clauses 2 and 7; Disclosure Letter para 3)
- **"Release to be provided following Completion" is unacceptable,** and it is inconsistent with the debt-free/cash-free basis.
- **Risks:**
  - The change-control clause (8.1) is likely triggered by the sale itself, which could put the facility into default and allow acceleration.
  - Security, potentially including PPSR-registered all-assets security and possibly security over the shares, would remain in place after Completion.
- **Require:**
  - A payout letter before Completion.
  - Repayment **out of the purchase price at Completion**, with the amount treated as Debt and deducted from price.
  - A deed of release and discharge under clause 9.2, and PPSR financing change statements and other releases, delivered **at** Completion as a Completion deliverable.
  - Confirmation that break costs, fees and accrued interest are included as Debt.

### 3.3 Employee Completion bonuses: AUD 420,000 (DD-005; Disclosure Letter para 5)
- **"A matter for the Seller" is misleading** if the Company is the paying employer. If so, the Company bears the cost after Completion, and therefore Wattlebridge does too. The bonuses are omitted from the funds flow.
- **On-costs are unaddressed.** These potentially include:
  - NSW payroll tax;
  - superannuation, depending on whether the bonuses are ordinary time earnings;
  - PAYG withholding;
  - workers' compensation premiums.
  - Total cost could be materially above AUD 420k.
- **Require:**
  - Treat the bonuses plus all on-costs as **Transaction Costs or Debt**, deducted from price or funded by the Seller.
  - Pay through Company payroll at Completion with correct withholding.
  - Itemise in the funds flow.
  - Add a specific indemnity.
- **Retention angle:** Check whether the "continued employment" conditions mean amounts may become payable after Completion. If so, quantify and deduct them now. We should also decide whether these employees are key-person retention risks.

### 3.4 Ironquay IP: SOW3 Project Materials (DD-004 cl 7.3; DD-010; clause 11.1; Disclosure Letter para 4)
- **The real risk is ownership, not the AUD 180k.** Transfer of the SOW3 materials is conditional on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180k open, and there is no evidence of payment or a confirmatory assignment.
- **What could go wrong:** If the SOW3 materials are embedded in the product, the Company may not own them. That exposes it to:
  - infringement or ownership claims;
  - injunction risk;
  - leverage by Ironquay over terms;
  - redevelopment costs.
- **An indemnity limited to "the SOW3 payment" does not cover any of this.**
- **Require:**
  - **A Completion deliverable or CP:** evidence of payment of all SOW3 fees, funded by the Seller or deducted from price, plus an executed **confirmatory IP assignment deed** from Ironquay, including moral rights consents where relevant.
  - **A broadened specific indemnity** covering all Loss arising from the Company not owning, or not having unencumbered rights to, the SOW3 materials. This includes third-party claims, redevelopment and replacement costs, and lost revenue.
  - That indemnity should be outside the general cap and thresholds, not qualified by disclosure, survive 6 or more years, and be backed by a specific retention.
- **Diligence:** Confirm what SOW3 delivered and where it sits in the product stack.

### 3.5 DD-006 export and privacy incident (clause 4.6; Schedule 6; Disclosure Letter para 6)
- **Contradiction:** The Seller Update says "not expected to be material." The Disclosure Letter says the scope, unauthorised access and notification requirements are **unknown**, and the investigation is preliminary.
- **The facts disclosed:** A download link to about 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) was sent to an unintended external address.
- **Regulatory exposure:** Under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, an entity that suspects an eligible data breach must complete a reasonable assessment, generally within 30 days. Given the 22 September date, that window has likely passed. We need to know whether an assessment was completed and whether the OAIC and individuals were notified.
- **Other exposure:**
  - Enhanced Privacy Act penalties for serious interferences.
  - Potential claims under the statutory privacy tort introduced by recent amendments.
  - Contractual notification breaches, for example under customer contracts possibly including Bluefen. Customer-relationship risk may exceed regulatory risk.
- **Require:**
  - An **immediate update** on investigation status, forensic findings, the NDB assessment and any notifications.
  - **Pre-Completion covenants:** complete a forensic investigation; make any required notifications in consultation with Wattlebridge; remediate.
  - **A specific indemnity** covering regulatory penalties to the extent lawfully indemnifiable, investigation and remediation costs, third-party and customer claims, and notification costs. It should be uncapped or separately capped, outside thresholds, not qualified by disclosure, survive 3 years or more, and be backed by a retention.
  - Specific privacy and data security warranties, brought down at Completion.

### 3.6 Sandbar renewals: 3 x AUD 110,000 = AUD 330,000 (DD-008; DD-011; Disclosure Letter para 8)
- **This is a red flag.** The Disclosure Letter says the three renewals are "related" and should be "read together for timing/scope." That suggests a single commitment may have been split into three parts. Possible reasons include:
  - staying under an approval threshold;
  - avoiding a material-contract or conduct-of-business threshold, potentially in the SPA itself.
- **The Seller has not shown** whether the renewals are ordinary course, terminable, prepaid or accrued, or unavoidable.
- **Require:**
  - Full details: dates, terms, termination rights, amounts paid or accrued, approvals, and any relationship between Sandbar and the Seller or its affiliates.
  - Aggregation language in the conduct-of-business covenant and in material-contract definitions, so that related contracts count together.
  - Unpaid amounts for pre-Completion periods treated as Debt or in working capital.
  - If the renewals were entered in breach of covenant or are not ordinary course, Seller responsibility or a price adjustment.

### 3.7 Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009): lower priority
- **The issue:** The Seller's framing ("notification only"; "consent not required merely because shares are sold") may be right, but it is the Seller's reading. Both disclosures are carefully worded.
- **Action:** Wattlebridge should review the change-of-control, deemed-assignment and notice provisions independently.
- **Require:**
  - A warranty that no consent is required and no right is triggered by the transaction.
  - Lease notification delivered as a Completion deliverable.

### 3.8 Funds flow
- **Gaps:** The funds flow omits the bonuses and has no visible Riverlark payout.
- **Require** a full funds flow, agreed before Completion, showing:
  - price;
  - less Debt (Riverlark payout and break costs);
  - less Transaction Costs (bonuses plus on-costs, Seller advisers if paid by the Company);
  - Ironquay settlement if Company-funded;
  - retentions and escrow;
  - net to Seller.
- It should be supported by payout letters and invoices.

---

## 4. Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Buyer response | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | General disclosure (Sch 7; DL 1.1–1.2) | Whole data room and public records | Specific, fair disclosure only; never qualifies fundamentals, tax or indemnities; no updating | **Critical** |
| 2 | Buyer knowledge (8.3) | Actual and constructive knowledge bars claims | Delete; knowledge does not affect claims (fallback: named individuals' actual knowledge) | **Critical** |
| 3 | Catch-all limitations (12.3/13; 9.3/12.8/20.5) | Limitations apply to all Claims | Limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims; carve out fraud, indemnities, tax, completion and price obligations | **Critical** |
| 4 | Fundamental warranties | Same cap and time limit | 100% price cap; 6+ years; no thresholds; independent title verification incl. share security | **Critical** |
| 5 | Riverlark (AUD 3.2m) | Release after Completion | Repaid from price at Completion as Debt; releases and PPSR discharges at Completion | **Critical** |
| 6 | Bluefen (30% revenue) | Reasonable endeavours; any written consent | Buyer-only-waivable CP; consent unconditional or acceptable to Buyer; 11.3 conditions met; all reasonable endeavours; sunset | **Critical** |
| 7 | Ironquay IP | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment | Payment plus confirmatory assignment at Completion; broad specific indemnity and retention | **High** |
| 8 | DD-006 privacy incident | "Not material" | Current update; NDB status; pre-Completion covenants; specific indemnity and retention | **High** |
| 9 | Bonuses (AUD 420k + on-costs) | "Matter for the Seller," omitted from funds flow | Deduct as Transaction Costs/Debt incl. payroll tax, super, PAYG; specific indemnity | **High** |
| 10 | Tax and IP regime | General regime | Standalone tax indemnity; quasi-fundamental IP warranties | **High** |
| 11 | Cap (20%) | AUD 4.8m | 30–50%, or W&I with seller-backed specific indemnities; retention or guarantee for security | **High** |
| 12 | Basket and de minimis | AUD 250k deductible; AUD 25k | Tipping basket around 0.5%; de minimis AUD 10–15k with aggregation of related claims | Medium |
| 13 | General time limit | 18 months | 24 months; tax for amendment period plus buffer | Medium |
| 14 | Sandbar (AUD 330k) | Ordinary course | Full information; aggregation rule; Debt or Seller responsibility if improper | Medium |
| 15 | Stale disclosure (22 Sept) | — | Updated Disclosure Letter; bring-down at Completion | Medium |
| 16 | Lease and Mossvale | No consent needed | Independent review; no-consent warranty; notice as deliverable | Low |

### Suggested next steps
1. **Information requests** to Seller counsel now on:
   - DD-006 investigation status and NDB assessment;
   - Bluefen consent correspondence and the 11.3 conditions;
   - Riverlark payout figure and security package, including any share security;
   - Ironquay payment status and SOW3 deliverables;
   - Sandbar contract details and approvals;
   - bonus on-cost calculations.
2. **Independent searches:** ASIC, PPSR (Seller and Company), and a reconciliation of the DD-012 register.
3. **W&I decision:** Decide early whether to pursue W&I insurance. It changes the cap and retention negotiation, and known matters will be excluded regardless.
4. **Mark-up order:** Lead with the structural points (items 1 to 4), since they determine the value of everything else. Then deal with the known-issue protections (items 5 to 9) as CPs, Completion deliverables, price deductions and specific indemnities, backed by retentions.

This analysis is based on the Seller's summary positions and should be checked against the full SPA text and data room documents once available.
=== END ADVICE ===
